question: m01
q: Are real wages going up? Compare wage growth from the ABS Wage Price Index with inflation.

transcript.answer:
**No. Real wages are falling again.** Wages are growing more slowly than prices, and the gap has been negative for about a year.

**Latest figures**
- **Wages:** The Wage Price Index (total hourly pay excluding bonuses, seasonally adjusted) rose **3.2% over the year to June quarter 2026**. That is the latest WPI release.
- **Prices:** Headline CPI was **3.8% over the year to June 2026**, so real wages fell by about **0.6 percentage points**.
- **Newest CPI:** Headline CPI was **4.0% in August 2026**, and the RBA's preferred trimmed mean was **3.6%**. Against the June-quarter wage growth of 3.2%, that is a gap of about −0.8 points on headline and −0.4 on trimmed mean. This mixes periods, so treat it as indicative until the September-quarter WPI is out.

**Wages versus CPI, year-on-year, at each quarter-end**

| Quarter | WPI | CPI | Real wage growth (pts) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sep 2024 | 3.6% | 2.8% | +0.8 |
| Dec 2024 | 3.2% | 2.4% | +0.8 |
| Mar 2025 | 3.5% | 2.4% | +1.1 |
| Jun 2025 | 3.4% | 2.1% | +1.3 |
| Sep 2025 | 3.3% | 3.6% | −0.3 |
| Dec 2025 | 3.4% | 3.8% | −0.4 |
| Mar 2026 | 3.2% | 4.6% | −1.4 |
| Jun 2026 | 3.2% | 3.8% | −0.6 |

The CPI figures up to June 2025 are the quarterly series. From September 2025 they are the monthly series for the quarter's last month. The two measures differ slightly. For September 2025 the quarterly CPI was 3.2%, which would make real wage growth about +0.1 rather than −0.3.

**What this shows**
- Real wages grew through 2024 and the first half of 2025. Wage growth of 3.2–3.6% outpaced inflation of about 2–2.8%.
- Real wages turned negative from the September 2025 quarter. CPI rose to 3.5–4.6%, and wage growth stayed at about 3.2–3.4%.
- The worst point was March 2026, when CPI hit 4.6% and real wages fell by about 1.4%. The squeeze has eased a little since, but inflation has picked up again in recent months.
- Wage growth has drifted down from 3.6% to 3.2% while inflation has risen. That is why the gap reopened.
